subject: Service-chain mapping + SOC2 evidence request — AzureStack
messages:
From: Jacob Miller <jacob.miller@azurestack.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Service-chain mapping + SOC2 evidence request

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. AzureStack is starting an RFP and the security team is confirming vendor coverage for our upcoming fiscal audit window (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). A couple of asks we need from Redwood to complete our assessment: 

- A service-chain mapping that shows which Redwood components touch customer data for the hosted API path (including gateway, inference runtime, KV cache, telemetry, backups). We need process-level owners and locations (cloud region).
- A subprocessor inventory that identifies which 3rd-party vendors handle encrypted-at-rest keys, backups, or are in the telemetry pipeline.
- A copy (or link) to your latest SOC 2 Type II report and any bridge letter or carve-out confirmation that covers cloud provider responsibilities for the same audit period above. If you provide a bridge letter, please note the cloud provider report(s) and exact date ranges covered.

If you could send an initial draft of the mapping and indicate whether this will be a subservice carve-out or carve-in for your cloud providers (we use AzureStack provider; we need the exact vendor report names) by EOD Tuesday 12/8 that would be ideal.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Jacob Miller
Security Engineer, AzureStack
Jacob.Miller@azurestack.com

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jacob Miller <jacob.miller@azurestack.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service-chain mapping + SOC2 evidence request

Jacob —

Appreciate the context and clear ask. Looping in Grace (Platform Security) and Neha (Compliance) to assemble the mapping and surface the SOC/bridge artifacts.

Grace / Neha — can you please: 
1) Pull together a one-page service-chain mapping for the hosted REST inference flow (API gateway -> auth -> routing -> inference runtime -> KV cache -> telemetry -> backups). Include which subprocessors (if any) handle encryption keys, telemetry ingestion, and long-term backups.
2) Confirm the exact SOC 2 Type II report(s) we are able to share and whether we have a bridge letter that explicitly ties our covered services to the cloud provider reports (specifically call out AzureStack or AzureStack partner reports and date ranges).
3) Attach the latest subprocessor manifest and a draft bridge letter if available.

I'll coordinate with legal if there are any redlines on the bridge wording. Jacob — we'll aim to send a draft by EOD Tue 12/8. If you need a call to walk through the mapping, tell us a 30-min window next week and we'll schedule.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

---

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Dec 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service-chain mapping + SOC2 evidence request

Folks —

Attached is an initial package:
- subprocessor_manifest_v2.xlsx (inventory + roles)
- service_chain_mapping_v1.pdf (diagram + owner list)
- bridge_letter_draft_azurestack.docx (working draft; still needs legal sign-off)

Quick notes from my review: 
- Our hosted API path (us-west-2) runs on Redwood-managed clusters; the inference runtime and KV cache are our code and managed by Redwood (no external subprocessor for runtime).
- Telemetry ingestion is forwarded to Telemetrix (telemetrix.io) for aggregation and long-term analytics; Telemetrix receives pseudonymized telemetry only — no plaintext customer content. Telemetrix is listed in the manifest with SOC 2 status & contract clause references.
- Backups are taken to an encrypted object storage bucket managed by AzureStack (vendor: AzureStack Storage Services); keys are customer-managed in KMS when customers opt in, otherwise keys are managed by AzureStack KMS. We note this distinction in the manifest.
- For the audit window you provided (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30) the relevant cloud provider coverage will be: AzureStack Cloud SOC 2 Type II report (period: 2025-07-01 through 2026-06-30). We will include a bridge letter that clarifies the gap between their report end-date and your audit window and how control ownership maps for the missing months.

Action items I own: finalize the mapping diagram and lock down the bridge wording with legal. Neha — can you confirm which provider reports we can attach and whether we need a signed letter vs. an attestation PDF?

Grace
Sr. Manager, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: subprocessor_manifest_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB), service_chain_mapping_v1.pdf (pdf, 180KB), bridge_letter_draft_azurestack.docx (docx, 28KB)

---

On Tue, 08 Dec 2026 14:42:00 -0800, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
To: Jacob Miller <jacob.miller@azurestack.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Re: Service-chain mapping + SOC2 evidence request

Jacob —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the package we discussed: service_chain_mapping_v1.pdf (diagram + owner mapping), subprocessor_manifest_v2.xlsx, and a working draft of the bridge letter. Summary below: 

- Covered components (hosted path us-west-2): API gateway (Redwood), auth/token service (Redwood), request router (Redwood), inference runtime (Redwood), KV cache (Redwood-managed Redis cluster), telemetry ingestion (Telemetrix — pseudonymized), backups (AzureStack Storage Services).
- Key custody: customers may opt for customer-managed keys in KMS; by default backups are encrypted with provider-managed keys. We flagged this in row 6 of the manifest.
- Cloud provider reports: AzureStack Cloud SOC 2 Type II (reporting period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30). We do not have an overlapping provider report that covers 2026-07-01 through 2026-09-30; the bridge letter explains control mapping for the latter quarter and references compensating controls (continuous backup verification, rolling snapshots, and our monitoring hooks).

Requested next steps from your side: 
1) Confirm whether AzureStack's report name and date range (above) meet your audit requirements or if you require a provider bridge signed by AzureStack.
2) Let us know if the auditors need a signed bridge letter vs. a Redwood-issued attestation. We can route the final bridge through legal and provide a DocuSign link to your security contact.

If you want a quick walk-through of the diagram I can join a 30-min slot tomorrow between 10:00-12:00 PST.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: service_chain_mapping_v1.pdf (pdf, 180KB), subprocessor_manifest_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB), bridge_letter_draft_azurestack.docx (docx, 28KB)

---

Jacob Miller <jacob.miller@azurestack.com> replied: "Thanks Karthik — this is really helpful. I'll confirm with our auditors whether a provider-signed bridge is required and loop back by EOD Friday. Could you forward the manifest as a CSV as well?"

End of thread.
